stories.headline: Brent crude slips to [$91.58]
stories.summary: Brent fell about 0.9% on 17 Nov to around $91.58 a barrel, while US WTI traded near $85. Expectations of stronger global supply outweighed Middle East tensions. The IEA sees a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter, and Goldman Sachs warned of a possible glut next year.

stories.headline: Two tankers hit in Hormuz - [engine room fires]
stories.summary: UKMTO reported two tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday 16 Nov. An outbound tanker was hit by a projectile around 05:58 UTC, causing an engine-room fire; all crew were accounted for. A second tanker was left disabled with an engine-room fire 7 nm north of Khasab, Oman, crew reported safe. Ship names were not released.

stories.headline: [227 ships] waiting outside the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: About 227 commercial ships are stationary at anchorages east of the strait, including Fujairah, Khor Fakkan, Sohar and Musandam. JMIC counts five attacks off Oman's Musandam Peninsula since 1 Nov. On 15 Nov, Indian authorities reported another vessel attacked in the Gulf, with all crew safe.

stories.headline: Towboat crew pulls [14 people] from the river
stories.summary: When the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck the paddle-wheeler American Heritage in New Orleans, about 100 of the 191 people aboard were still on board as it rolled over. A five-member towboat crew from Canal Barge Co. pulled 14 people from the water. 32 went to hospital and no one died. NTSB plans a preliminary report in 30 days.

stories.headline: Ice nearly stops Korea's [first Arctic box ship]
stories.summary: The 2,758-TEU PanStar Acro met drifting ice south of Wrangel Island on South Korea's first Northern Sea Route container trial. Captain Seo Myeong-won considered turning back but waited for daylight, and a route opened about three hours later. PanStar is now weighing a sale, possibly back to HMM.

stories.headline: Samsung Heavy wins [$257m] LNG carrier order
stories.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries disclosed on 16 Nov a contract worth about $257 million for one LNG carrier, ordered by an unnamed Oceania-based shipowner. Shipbuilding sources tie the order to Celsius Shipping, which has been adding large LNG carriers at the Korean yard.

stories.headline: Black Sea ship attacks pass [300] this year
stories.summary: Attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea have passed 300 this year, disrupting trade in the region. Vessel entries through the Bosporus fell 41% year on year in October. Romania and Bulgaria have reported drone strikes on ships near their coasts in recent weeks.

stories.headline: US-China truce pauses [ship fees] to Jan 2027
stories.summary: The US and China formally extended their trade truce to 10 January 2027. It keeps reduced tariffs and the suspension of US fees on China-linked vessels in place, and extends 178 Section 301 tariff exclusions. Separately, the White House is reported to be preparing to extend the Jones Act waiver.

stories.headline: Box lines' profits lifted by [higher rates]
stories.summary: Stronger freight rates lifted third-quarter profits at Evergreen, Wan Hai, HMM, CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd. Carriers still warn of geopolitical disruption and high operating costs. The container ship orderbook is about 43-46% of the fleet, raising overcapacity worries from 2027.
